module: Module 5: Data Subject Rights Basic Level 1 Set

items.lesson_concept: The Right to be Informed is the most basic right of a data subject. It guarantees that individuals have the right to know whether their personal data shall be, are being, or have been processed.
items.question_text: Which fundamental right ensures that an individual knows whether a company is collecting and processing their personal data?
items.explanation: The Right to be Informed is the foundational right that guarantees transparency, ensuring people know if their data is being processed.

items.lesson_concept: To effectively uphold the Right to be Informed, an organization must notify the data subject of the processing details *before* their personal data enters the processing system.
items.question_text: When must an organization fulfill the data subject's 'Right to be Informed' regarding how their data will be used?
options: Only when the data subject formally asks for it.
After the data has already been sold to a third party.
Before the entry of their personal data into the processing system.
items.correct_answer: Before the entry of their personal data into the processing system.
items.explanation: Data subjects must be informed before their data is collected and processed so they can make an educated decision.

items.lesson_concept: The Right to Access gives data subjects the right to demand reasonable access to the specific contents of their personal data that an organization holds.
items.question_text: Which right allows you to ask a company for a physical or digital copy of the personal information they currently hold about you?
items.explanation: The Right to Access empowers individuals to inspect and obtain copies of the personal data an organization has on file.

items.lesson_concept: Under the Right to Access, a data subject can also demand to know the names and addresses of the third parties (recipients) to whom their personal data has been disclosed.
items.question_text: Aside from seeing the data itself, what else can a data subject demand to know under the 'Right to Access'?
options: The salaries of the IT department.
The names and addresses of third parties to whom their data was disclosed.
items.correct_answer: The names and addresses of third parties to whom their data was disclosed.
items.explanation: The Right to Access includes knowing who else has received or viewed your personal data.

items.lesson_concept: The Right to Object gives data subjects the right to say 'no' to the processing of their personal data, including the right to withdraw consent.
items.question_text: Which data subject right allows an individual to refuse or withhold their consent to the processing of their personal data?
items.explanation: The Right to Object is the right to say 'no' and withhold or withdraw consent to data processing.

items.lesson_concept: A data subject has an absolute right to object to the processing of their data for direct marketing, automated processing, or profiling.
items.question_text: If a user no longer wants to receive promotional sales emails from a clothing store, which right are they exercising when they click 'Unsubscribe'?
items.explanation: Unsubscribing from direct marketing is a direct application of the Right to Object.

items.lesson_concept: The Right to Rectify allows a data subject to dispute inaccuracies or errors in their personal data and demand that the organization correct it.
items.question_text: If you discover that your bank has listed your birthdate incorrectly on your profile, which right allows you to demand that they fix the error?
items.explanation: The Right to Rectify (or correct) ensures that data subjects can fix false, outdated, or inaccurate information.

items.lesson_concept: When a data subject successfully exercises their Right to Rectify, the PIC must also ensure that third parties who previously received the erroneous data are informed of the correction.
items.question_text: What must a company do after correcting a user's inaccurate data under the Right to Rectify?
options: Ensure third parties who previously received the incorrect data are informed of the correction.
Charge the user an administrative correction fee.
Report the user to the police.
items.correct_answer: Ensure third parties who previously received the incorrect data are informed of the correction.
items.explanation: To fully rectify the error, the correction must cascade to any third parties who were given the bad data.

items.lesson_concept: The Right to Erasure or Blocking gives data subjects the right to suspend, withdraw, or order the blocking, removal, or destruction of their personal data from an organization's system.
items.question_text: Which right enables a data subject to demand that a company completely delete their personal data from its database?
items.explanation: The Right to Erasure (also known as the right to be forgotten) allows for the deletion or removal of personal data.

items.lesson_concept: The Right to Erasure can be invoked when the personal data is incomplete, outdated, false, unlawfully obtained, or no longer necessary for its original purpose.
items.question_text: Under what circumstance can you lawfully demand the erasure of your personal data?
options: Only when you are moving to another country.
When the data is no longer necessary for the purposes for which it was originally collected.
Only if the company is bankrupt.
When you want to evade paying a legitimate financial debt.
items.correct_answer: When the data is no longer necessary for the purposes for which it was originally collected.
items.explanation: Data subjects can invoke erasure when the organization has no more legitimate, lawful reason to hold the data.

items.lesson_concept: The Right to Data Portability allows data subjects to obtain their personal data in an electronic or structured format so they can transfer it to another system.
items.question_text: Which right specifically requires an organization to provide your data in a commonly used, machine-readable electronic format?
items.explanation: Data Portability is unique because it specifically requires the data to be delivered in an electronic, interoperable format.

items.lesson_concept: The primary goal of the Right to Data Portability is to empower users and prevent 'vendor lock-in' by allowing them to easily move their data between different service providers.
items.question_text: What is the primary consumer benefit of the Right to Data Portability?
options: It prevents 'vendor lock-in' by allowing users to easily move their digital data to a competing service.
It forces companies to print all records on paper.
It allows users to delete their online history.
It makes data immune to computer viruses.
items.correct_answer: It prevents 'vendor lock-in' by allowing users to easily move their digital data to a competing service.
items.explanation: Portability allows users to take their own electronic data and move it to a new service provider without being locked into the old one.

items.lesson_concept: The Right to File a Complaint allows data subjects to seek the help of the National Privacy Commission (NPC) if they feel their privacy rights have been violated.
items.question_text: If a company ignores your request to delete your unlawfully obtained data, which right allows you to escalate the issue to the government?
items.explanation: Data subjects have the right to file a formal complaint with the NPC if a Personal Information Controller violates the DPA.

items.lesson_concept: Complaints regarding data privacy violations are filed with the National Privacy Commission (NPC), the agency mandated to enforce the DPA.
items.question_text: To which specific government agency should a data subject file a formal complaint regarding a privacy violation?
items.explanation: The National Privacy Commission is the primary adjudicatory body for privacy complaints.

items.lesson_concept: The Right to Damages ensures that a data subject can be indemnified (compensated) for any harm or injury sustained due to a privacy violation.
items.question_text: Which right entitles a data subject to financial compensation if they suffer harm due to a company leaking their sensitive personal information?
items.explanation: The Right to Damages provides for indemnification for any damages sustained due to DPA violations.

items.lesson_concept: Data subject rights are transmissible. This means that if a data subject dies or becomes incapacitated, their lawful heirs can invoke these rights on their behalf.
items.question_text: If a data subject passes away, what happens to their data privacy rights under the DPA?
options: The rights are passed to the government.
The rights are transmissible and can be invoked by their lawful heirs and assigns.
The rights are sold to the highest bidder.
items.correct_answer: The rights are transmissible and can be invoked by their lawful heirs and assigns.
items.explanation: Section 17 explicitly states that the lawful heirs and assigns may invoke the rights of the data subject after their death or incapacity.

items.lesson_concept: The rights guaranteed by the Data Privacy Act are fundamental. A company cannot force a user to sign a contract completely giving up their privacy rights.
items.question_text: Can an online app force you to sign a contract that completely waives all of your data privacy rights forever?
options: No, fundamental data subject rights under the DPA cannot be completely waived through a contract.
Yes, if the app is free to use.
items.correct_answer: No, fundamental data subject rights under the DPA cannot be completely waived through a contract.
items.explanation: Data privacy is a fundamental human right. Contracts that force a complete waiver of these rights are void against public policy.

items.lesson_concept: While the Right to Access is guaranteed, a Personal Information Controller (PIC) may charge a reasonable administrative fee to provide physical copies of the data.
items.question_text: Is a company allowed to charge a small administrative fee if you request multiple printed copies of your personal data under the Right to Access?
options: No, it must always be entirely free.
Yes, a PIC may charge a reasonable fee to cover the administrative costs of providing the information.
No, unless authorized by the President.
Yes, they can charge up to 50% of your salary.
items.correct_answer: Yes, a PIC may charge a reasonable fee to cover the administrative costs of providing the information.
items.explanation: NPC guidelines allow for a reasonable administrative fee to cover the physical/administrative cost of fulfilling access requests.

items.lesson_concept: Under the Right to be Informed, the data subject has the right to know the exact identity and contact details of the Personal Information Controller.
items.question_text: Which right ensures that a user knows exactly which company is responsible for collecting their data and how to contact them?
items.explanation: The Right to be Informed mandates that the identity and contact details of the PIC are made known to the data subject.

items.lesson_concept: The Data Privacy Act outlines eight (8) specific fundamental rights granted to data subjects to give them control over their personal information.
items.question_text: What is the primary purpose of the 'Data Subject Rights' outlined in the Data Privacy Act?
options: To give the government control over citizen data.
To empower individuals and give them control over how their personal information is processed.
To allow companies to sell data freely.
items.correct_answer: To empower individuals and give them control over how their personal information is processed.
items.explanation: The fundamental goal of data subject rights is to put control of personal information back into the hands of the individual.
